A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REPA work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including retained material that is relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiT/SiT training experiments, representation analyses and ablations on ImageNet, with additional quantitative and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds results for SigLIP alignment, ImageNet 512×512, MS-COCO text-to-image generation and feature-map analysis.

M1.justification: The REPA alignment loss and projection mechanism remain unchanged. Appendix K adds a text-conditioned model implementation using MMDiT joint image/text attention and CLIP caption embeddings, extending the previously evaluated DiT/SiT implementations.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates generation on ImageNet 256×256. v2 retains this coverage and adds ImageNet 512×512 and MS-COCO text-to-image generation in Appendices J and K, substantially extending resolution, represented scenes and conditioning requirements.

E2.justification: The existing ImageNet 256×256 comparator sets are retained. New Table 12 introduces vanilla MMDiT controls and reported comparisons with text-to-image methods including AttnGAN, DM-GAN, VQ-Diffusion, DF-GAN, XMC-GAN, Frido and LAFITE, substantially expanding the comparison methods.

E3.justification: The new MS-COCO protocol uses 150K training iterations, CFG 2.0 and ODE-50/SDE-250 evaluation; the 512×512 experiment uses larger latent inputs. Appendix D also revises Figure 3/SiT-B alignment depths from 4/8 to 8/4 and Table 4 settings from 24 to 28 layers, width 1024 to 1152, and NT-Xent to cosine similarity. These reported revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 extends the encoder ablation with SigLIP, adds an encoder-pretraining dataset analysis in Table 6, and provides layer-wise PCA feature maps at several noise levels in Figure 38. Figure 11 extends the training-convergence analysis to CFG. These supplement the retained ablations without replacing their central questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing tabulated numbers are retained, while substantial new results appear. Table 2 adds SigLIP FID 10.2. Table 12 reports MMDiT FIDs without/with REPA of 6.05/4.73 under ODE-50 and 5.30/4.14 under SDE-250. Table 11 adds ImageNet 512×512 results, including REPA FID 2.08 at 200 epochs. These are newly reported experiments, alongside additional convergence and feature-map findings.

T1.justification: The diffusion/stochastic-interpolant formulations, REPA objective and CKNNA definitions are retained. Equation 8 receives a parenthesis correction, but no mathematical reasoning, assumptions, formal properties or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the central claims that representation alignment improves diffusion-transformer training and generation, including the greater-than-17.5× speedup and FID 1.42 headline results. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly argues that gains do not simply reflect ImageNet data leakage. Appendix M specifies untested pixel-space, video, large-scale text-to-image and time-varying-weight directions. Appendix J adds a four-metric superiority interpretation, although Table 11 shows tied precision at 100 epochs and worse sFID and precision at 200 epochs.

D1.justification: v2 discloses encoder pretraining datasets and the absence of ImageNet fine-tuning, clarifies that Figure 3 evaluates layers of one trained network, and documents the new resolution processing and MMDiT/CLIP configuration. Appendix D revises configuration entries. Hardware information and the promise of future code/checkpoint release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: References are added for SigLIP, MS-COCO and the new text-to-image comparators. The core positioning against two-stage representation-conditioned generators and auxiliary self-supervision remains stable. Much of the denoising-as-self-supervision discussion moves from Section 5 to Appendix I rather than being newly introduced.

P1.justification: v2 shortens Section 5, relocates part of its discussion to Appendix I, adds appendix sections and cross-references, and makes localized caption and prose edits. Figure 10's mistaken SiT identification is corrected to DiT. Most of the main narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with encoder-provenance and new benchmark tables, a CFG convergence plot, higher-resolution samples, paired text-to-image examples and PCA maps (Tables 6, 11–12; Figures 11, 36–38). Table 2 and Figure 5 gain SigLIP entries. Existing appendix image galleries are preserved and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical generality beyond v1's single-resolution, class-conditioned ImageNet setting, especially through matched MMDiT comparisons on MS-COCO. Higher-resolution validation, repaired configuration inconsistencies and explicit applicability limits also improve the paper. Appendix J's overbroad four-metric claim is a reporting weakness, but it does not outweigh the substantial gain in validation and reproducibility.
